accepted.s: The Warehousing (Development and Regulation) Act, 2007 came into force on:
accepted.x: The Warehousing (Development and Regulation) Act, 2007 came into force on 25 October 2010.
accepted.tq: Use precise date discrimination between closely related institutional milestones.
accepted.sec: Warehousing - WDR Act 2007, WDRA, NWRs, CWC

accepted.s: The Warehousing Development and Regulatory Authority (WDRA) was constituted on:
accepted.x: WDRA was constituted on 26 October 2010 under the Warehousing (Development and Regulation) Act, 2007.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the date of commencement of an Act from the date of constitution of the authority.
accepted.sec: Warehousing - WDR Act 2007, WDRA, NWRs, CWC

accepted.s:
With reference to Negotiable Warehouse Receipts (NWRs), consider the following statements:
1. NWRs are notified for 143 agricultural commodities.
2. NWRs are notified for 24 horticultural commodities.
3. NWRs are notified for 9 non-agricultural commodities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: NWRs are notified for 143 agricultural, 24 horticultural and 9 non-agricultural commodities.
accepted.tq: Retain all three category-wise numerical figures before selecting the combined option.
accepted.sec: Warehousing - WDR Act 2007, WDRA, NWRs, CWC

accepted.s: The e-NWR is best described as:
o: An electronic market-fee receipt issued by an Agricultural Market Committee
A warehouse construction grant issued to PACS
A digital subsidy certificate issued by NAFED for MSP procurement
An electronic ownership certificate for goods stored in a WDRA-accredited warehouse
accepted.x: An e-NWR is an electronic ownership certificate for goods held in a WDRA-accredited warehouse.
accepted.tq: Test the exact meaning of a specialised institutional term rather than its similar-sounding alternatives.
accepted.sec: Warehousing - WDR Act 2007, WDRA, NWRs, CWC

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding e-NWRs is correct?
o: They cannot be used as collateral for loans.
They can be issued only for non-agricultural commodities.
They are issued exclusively by the Central Warehousing Corporation.
They are tradable on the e-NAM platform.
accepted.x: Electronic Negotiable Warehouse Receipts are tradable on e-NAM and can support pledge finance.
accepted.tq: Separate the actual function of a digital instrument from restrictive distractors.
accepted.sec: Warehousing - WDR Act 2007, WDRA, NWRs, CWC

accepted.s: The e-Kisan Upaj Nidhi portal was launched on:
accepted.x: e-Kisan Upaj Nidhi, a WDRA digital gateway, was launched on 4 March 2024.
accepted.tq: Numerical recall of a scheme-launch date.
accepted.sec: Warehousing - WDR Act 2007, WDRA, NWRs, CWC

accepted.s: Loans against WDRA-accredited warehouse receipts are eligible for interest subvention at what rate and for what period after harvest?
accepted.x: Interest subvention is available at 7% for post-harvest loans against WDRA-accredited receipts for up to six months.
accepted.tq: Match the rate with the duration instead of treating either figure in isolation.
accepted.sec: Warehousing - WDR Act 2007, WDRA, NWRs, CWC

accepted.s: The Central Warehousing Corporation (CWC) was set up on 2 March 1957 under the:
o: Agricultural Produce (Development and Warehousing) Corporations Act, 1956
accepted.x: CWC was established on 2 March 1957 under the Agricultural Produce (Development and Warehousing) Corporations Act, 1956. It is now associated with the Warehousing Corporations Act, 1962.
accepted.tq: Use the parent-Act trap by distinguishing the original legal basis from the later Act.
accepted.sec: Warehousing - WDR Act 2007, WDRA, NWRs, CWC

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the pilot of the World's Largest Grain Storage Plan in the Cooperative Sector?
o: It covered 11 PACS in 11 States with a capacity of 9,750 MT.
It covered 11 PACS in one State with a capacity of 9,750 lakh MT.
It covered 313 PACS in 11 States with a capacity of 1.80 lakh MT.
It covered 22 PACS in 22 States with a capacity of 9,750 MT.
accepted.x: The pilot involved 11 PACS in 11 States and had a storage capacity of 9,750 MT.
accepted.tq: Pair the number of institutions, States and capacity without mixing pilot and later figures.
accepted.sec: Warehousing - WDR Act 2007, WDRA, NWRs, CWC

accepted.s: The World's Largest Grain Storage Plan in the Cooperative Sector is implemented by the NCDC in association with:
accepted.x: NCDC implements the plan with NABARD, CWC and FCI.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure institutional association and reject substituted agencies.
accepted.sec: Warehousing - WDR Act 2007, WDRA, NWRs, CWC

accepted.s: The cooperative-sector grain storage plan seeks to build godowns and processing units at the PACS level by converging:
o: 10 schemes, including Operation Greens and FCI procurement
8 schemes, including the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund and Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure
3 schemes, including PM-AASHA and TOP to TOTAL
accepted.x: The plan converges eight schemes, including the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund and Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure scheme, to create PACS-level facilities.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact convergence count and the two named component schemes.
accepted.sec: Warehousing - WDR Act 2007, WDRA, NWRs, CWC

accepted.s: By July 2026, the cooperative-sector grain storage plan had reached which of the following levels?
o: 313 PACS and more than 1.80 lakh MT
accepted.x: By July 2026, the plan covered 313 PACS and more than 1.80 lakh MT of capacity.
accepted.tq: Distinguish later implementation figures from the pilot figures and AP warehouse statistics.
accepted.sec: Warehousing - WDR Act 2007, WDRA, NWRs, CWC

accepted.s: Under the cooperative-sector grain storage plan, the AMI subsidy and margin-money requirement were respectively changed to:
accepted.x: The AMI subsidy was raised from 25% to 33.33%, while the margin-money requirement was reduced from 20% to 10%.
accepted.tq: Compare both before-and-after figures to avoid reversing the policy changes.
accepted.sec: Warehousing - WDR Act 2007, WDRA, NWRs, CWC

accepted.s: Which combination of measures reduces the effective interest for PACS under the cooperative-sector grain storage plan to 1%?
o: 25% AMI subsidy and NAFED procurement only
WDRA accreditation and e-NAM trading alone
3% AIF subvention and NABARD refinance, together with the revised AMI support
7% interest subvention and FCI procurement, without NABARD refinance
accepted.x: The effective interest falls to 1% through the revised AMI support combined with 3% AIF subvention and NABARD refinance.
accepted.tq: Combine separate policy instruments to identify the resulting financing benefit.
accepted.sec: Warehousing - WDR Act 2007, WDRA, NWRs, CWC

accepted.s: According to the AP warehouse data for 2025-26, which of the following is correct?
o: There were 626 godowns with 5.66 lakh MT capacity, of which 1,052 were operational.
There were 643 godowns with 5.92 lakh MT capacity, of which 1,052 were operational.
There were 1,052 godowns with 9.65 lakh MT capacity, of which 626 were operational with 5.66 lakh MT capacity.
There were 1,052 godowns with 9.65 lakh MT capacity, of which 643 were operational with 5.92 lakh MT capacity.
accepted.x: In 2025-26, AP had 1,052 godowns with total capacity of 9.65 lakh MT; 643 were operational with 5.92 lakh MT capacity.
accepted.tq: Keep total and operational warehouse figures separate while comparing two years.
accepted.sec: Warehousing - WDR Act 2007, WDRA, NWRs, CWC

accepted.s: NAFED is best described as the:
o: Central agency for food-grain storage alone
accepted.x: NAFED is the apex agricultural cooperative marketing body and was set up in 1958.
accepted.tq: Test the exact institutional role rather than a related marketing function.
accepted.sec: Cooperative marketing - NAFED, apex cooperative, State marketing federations  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Under the Price Support Scheme of PM-AASHA, procurement at MSP covers:
accepted.x: The Price Support Scheme procures pulses, oilseeds and copra at MSP.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the commodity basket of PM-AASHA and that of Operation Greens.
accepted.sec: Cooperative marketing - NAFED, apex cooperative, State marketing federations  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: From 2024-25, procurement under the PM-AASHA Price Support Scheme is permitted up to what proportion of production?
accepted.x: From 2024-25, procurement under the Price Support Scheme is permitted up to 25% of production.
accepted.tq: Recall the policy ceiling rather than choosing a familiar procurement percentage.
accepted.sec: Cooperative marketing - NAFED, apex cooperative, State marketing federations  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: In Andhra Pradesh, MARKFED is the:
o: State agency for tribal produce marketing
accepted.x: MARKFED is the apex body of cooperative marketing societies in Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Identify the state-level cooperative apex body from closely related national agencies.
accepted.sec: Cooperative marketing - NAFED, apex cooperative, State marketing federations  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: TRIFED — Price Support Scheme for copra
accepted.x: AP MARKFED has a ₹3,000 crore Price Stabilisation Fund. The other organisations have different functions or jurisdictions.
accepted.tq: Use the organisation-function association and reject swapped institutional roles.
accepted.sec: Cooperative marketing - NAFED, apex cooperative, State marketing federations  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The 2025 turnover and profit of District Cooperative Marketing Societies (DCMS) in Andhra Pradesh were respectively:
accepted.x: AP DCMS recorded a 2025 turnover of ₹13,391.12 lakh and a profit of ₹720.29 lakh.
accepted.tq: Keep turnover and profit in their proper order and units.
accepted.sec: Cooperative marketing - NAFED, apex cooperative and State marketing federations  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: TRIFED is primarily associated with:
o: Price support for oilseeds and copra
accepted.x: TRIFED is concerned with marketing tribal produce. It was established in 1987 under the framework associated with the Multi-State Co-operative Societies Act, 1984.
accepted.tq: Apply the body-function test to distinguish TRIFED from agricultural marketing agencies.
accepted.sec: Cooperative marketing - NAFED, apex cooperative, State marketing federations  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following is a major effect of middlemen and brokers in agricultural marketing?
o: They ensure that farmers receive the entire consumer rupee.
They increase the density of regulated markets.
They raise consumer prices and add red tape.
They reduce consumer prices by eliminating all transaction costs.
accepted.x: Middlemen and brokers can raise consumer prices and add red tape to the marketing process.
accepted.tq: Choose the practical consequence of intermediaries rather than an absolute claim about marketing.
accepted.sec: Problems - intermediaries, price spread, distress sale, poor storage, market density  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Approximately what proportion of built storage capacity is reported to remain idle, contributing to distress sale?
accepted.x: About 40% of built storage lies idle, which contributes to distress sale by limiting usable storage access.
accepted.tq: Link the numerical estimate with its stated economic consequence.
accepted.sec: Problems - intermediaries, price spread, distress sale, poor storage, market density  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The National Commission on Farmers suggested that a regulated market should be available within approximately what distance of farmers?
accepted.x: The National Commission on Farmers suggested a regulated market within about 5 km of farmers.
accepted.tq: Recall the recommended market-density distance as a direct quantitative fact.
accepted.sec: Problems - intermediaries, price spread, distress sale, poor storage, market density  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Price spread in agricultural marketing is calculated as:
accepted.x: Price spread is the consumer price minus the price received by the farmer; it indicates marketing margins and the share of intermediaries.
accepted.tq: Use the formula direction carefully to avoid reversing the two prices.
accepted.sec: Farmer's share in consumer rupee - price spread studies  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Price spread primarily measures:
o: The amount of MSP announced by the government
The storage capacity of regulated markets
Marketing margins and the share of middlemen
accepted.x: Price spread measures the difference between the consumer price and farmer's price, reflecting marketing margins and the share of middlemen.
accepted.tq: Infer the economic meaning of a calculated difference instead of merely recalling its formula.
accepted.sec: Farmer's share in consumer rupee - price spread studies  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Operation Greens initially covered which group of crops?
accepted.x: Operation Greens initially covered Tomato, Onion and Potato, commonly referred to as TOP.
accepted.tq: Discriminate the TOP crop basket from the later TOTAL expansion and PM-AASHA commodities.
accepted.sec: Operation Greens - announcing budget, TOP to TOTAL, subsidy pattern  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Operation Greens was modelled on the lines of:
accepted.x: Operation Greens was modelled on the lines of Operation Flood.
accepted.tq: Use the named-policy association rather than selecting another well-known government programme.
accepted.sec: Operation Greens - announcing budget, TOP to TOTAL, subsidy pattern  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Operation Greens seeks to address the seasonal and regional nature of TOP crops because they are:
o: Produced only for export and not for domestic consumption
Grown only in regulated market areas
Grown seasonally and regionally but consumed throughout the year
Produced throughout the year and consumed only seasonally
accepted.x: Tomato, onion and potato are grown seasonally and regionally but are consumed throughout the year, creating price fluctuations.
accepted.tq: Apply the production-consumption mismatch to identify the policy rationale.
accepted.sec: Operation Greens - announcing budget, TOP to TOTAL, subsidy pattern  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a major means through which Operation Greens aims to curb erratic prices?
o: Complete abolition of all agricultural markets
accepted.x: Operation Greens uses FPOs, agri-logistics, processing and professional management to address price volatility; abolition of all agricultural markets is not an objective stated for the scheme.
accepted.tq: Find the option outside the stated package of interventions.
accepted.sec: Operation Greens - announcing budget, TOP to TOTAL, subsidy pattern  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Operation Greens is implemented by the:
o: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution
Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
accepted.x: Operation Greens is implemented by the Ministry of Food Processing Industries.
accepted.tq: Apply the ministry-ownership trap by separating food processing from agriculture and food distribution.
accepted.sec: Operation Greens - announcing budget, TOP to TOTAL, subsidy pattern  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The extension of Operation Greens from TOP to all fruits and vegetables took place in:
accepted.x: The scheme was extended from TOP to all fruits and vegetables in 2020 under the Atmanirbhar Bharat package.
accepted.tq: Place the first expansion before the later extension to 22 perishable crops.
accepted.sec: Operation Greens - announcing budget, TOP to TOTAL, subsidy pattern  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: In the Union Budget 2021-22, Operation Greens was extended to:
accepted.x: The Union Budget 2021-22 extended Operation Greens to 22 perishable crops.
accepted.tq: Retain the exact later-expansion number separately from the all-fruits-and-vegetables extension.
accepted.sec: Operation Greens - announcing budget, TOP to TOTAL, subsidy pattern  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Under the short-term interventions of Operation Greens, subsidy on transport and storage is provided at:
accepted.x: Short-term interventions under Operation Greens provide a 50% subsidy on transport and storage.
accepted.tq: Match the subsidy percentage with the intervention category.
accepted.sec: Operation Greens - announcing budget, TOP to TOTAL, subsidy pattern  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: For long-term value-chain projects under Operation Greens, the grant-in-aid is:
accepted.x: Long-term value-chain projects receive 50% grant-in-aid generally and 70% grant-in-aid when implemented by FPOs.
accepted.tq: Compare the general and FPO-specific rates without reversing their order.
accepted.sec: Operation Greens - announcing budget, TOP to TOTAL, subsidy pattern  [APPSC, GROUP-II]
